Kiwoo Shin · Synthetic experiments

ROOMGRAPH / REAL-WORLD PILOT

From simulated rooms to a real RGB-D capture.

ARKitScenes validation capture 42445021 · 240 input views · frozen synthetic edge model · measured depth and supplied estimated camera poses.

Calibration is part of the experiment. We compare nominal estimates with deliberately injected pose, calibration, depth-scale and synchronization errors. Confidence + multi-view filtering rejects unsupported observations; it does not correct drift.

Recorded movement and learned overlays

Five selected frames per playback second; original timestamps are displayed. The top-down background is the final observed map, not a claim of progressive complete reconstruction. Images are rotated upright using dataset metadata, with matching camera calibration.

Inspect the observed 3D map

Drag or use arrow keys to rotate; scroll to zoom. Mint points are learned structural-edge predictions. Colored surfaces come from measured depth.

What happens when calibration is wrong?

Jitter uses three fixed seeds; bars show means and standard deviations. Other cases are deterministic. Translation and rotation jitter scales are per axis. The same RGB predictions and selected input frames are reused in every replay.

These are surface-agreement scores against the available reference-depth subset, not architectural-edge accuracy or full-building reconstruction scores. Reference views are withheld from fusion; their world placement still uses supplied ARKit pose estimates. Correct reconstructed surfaces outside reference coverage can lower precision.

Measured complete experiment: 108.3s, including input validation, inference, reference construction and 24 fusion evaluations; media generation excluded. Median model forward: 7.66ms. No retraining.

Scope and next steps

  • One development capture; no real-data retraining or threshold selection.
  • Nominal ARKit poses are estimates, not independently measured ground truth.
  • Reference is the union of held-out FARO-derived depth views, lifted using nominal ARKit calibration/poses. Not a separately registered full-scene laser benchmark.
  • Surface metrics are not architectural-edge accuracy; no typed real edge labels are available.
  • Confidence and multi-view filtering do not correct systematic pose/calibration errors.
  • Offline replay; no active navigation, humanoid self-mask or completed room shell.

The next correction stage should jointly refine overlapping-frame poses using robust geometric residuals, retain pose priors in ambiguous views, and re-fuse original observations after corrections. Persistent calibration bias needs calibration refinement; averaging alone cannot remove it.

Data: ARKitScenes, Baruch et al. (2021). Dataset license. RoomGraph source. Full captures, predictions and visualization artifacts remain local.
